title: The selection reply re-sends the fleet-wide project_roots map every 30 s, and its per-response timestamp defeats the companion's write-on-change cache
what: GET /api/v1/selection/<editor>?machine= answers with every sticky Resolve-project mapping in the fleet (project_roots grows with every mapping and is pruned only by an admin delete) plus generated_at stamped to the second. The companion fetches every 30 s and its AUDIT_2 P11 write-on-change guard compares the whole response including the timestamp, so every fetch is a full download and a tmp+replace rewrite of selection.json.
cost: 2,880 fetches/day per machine. 100 mappings: 23 KB per reply (measured) = 66 MB/day down and 66 MB/day of editor SSD writes per machine. 500 projects: 104 KB = 300 MB/day per machine, 6 GB/day across 20 machines, for an answer that changes a few times a week.
evidence: probe_views.py: _selection_view 23,054 B (project_roots 18,770 B) at 100 projects, 103,791 B (95,170 B) at 500; selection.py:350-390 compares response == self._last_written on the parsed dict that always carries a new generated_at.
fix: Companion: compare the response with generated_at removed. Dashboard: strong ETag over the response minus generated_at, 304 on If-None-Match; a 304 counts as a successful live fetch (comp-sync-14 stamp), never as unreachable (AUDIT_2 CORE-H9), and the editor-keyed cache rule (bug-comp-syncthing-6) is unchanged.

title: The report holds the database write lock across a filesystem walk of the Projects tree (CR-379 rival check)
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/api.py:10981 (holds.begin = BEGIN IMMEDIATE), api.py:11122 (_auto_map_has_rival), api.py:4327-4357 (provision.scan_unregistered_dirs, 60 s cache)
what: The auto-map block runs after BEGIN IMMEDIATE and before the first commit at 11376. On a cache miss _auto_map_has_rival os.walks projects_dir (depth up to 8, pruned at markers) with the write lock held. When a rival is found the mapping is not written, so the walk repeats after every 60 s cache expiry for as long as that Resolve project stays open.
cost: Measured 46-51 ms for a warm synthetic 500-project tree on local SSD; on the NAS with a cold ARC or during a scrub estimated hundreds of ms to seconds, during which the collector, session touches and every other machine's report wait on the 5 s busy_timeout (the 2026-09-03 database-is-locked shape). Ordering confirmed; NAS cost estimated.
evidence: Read of api_report statement order; _WriteHolds.begin executes BEGIN IMMEDIATE (api.py:133-139); timed scan_unregistered_dirs; api.py:10973-10976 already states no write transaction may be open across a lookup (LG-4).
ledger: new; related to CR-379 (fixed) and CR-351
fix: Compute detected_slug, the confident match and the rival verdict before holds.begin (reads plus a walk), keep only db.sticky_project_root inside the transaction. Keep the rival refusal, the 60 s cache and 'tree unreadable means ask'.

title: standins_known re-sends up to 200 archive paths on every report reply to every machine
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/api.py:11777; dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/db.py:11348 (GROUP BY over all of broll_standins with a sort, per report)
what: The reply always carries the full fleet stand-in list whether or not it changed since the last reply to that machine.
cost: Reply 292 B -> 14,181 B with 200 stand-ins (measured). Per machine 20 MB/day at the 60 s cadence, 242 MB/day at the 5 s active cadence, plus a companion JSON parse per tick. Live stand-in count not read (rule), so daily figures scale linearly from 200.
ledger: related to wire-3 (bug-hunt-2026-09-18b, correctness of the same list)
fix: Add standins_known.sig; the companion echoes the last sig it applied; send rels only when the sigs differ. Absent stays 'does not know', empty stays 'none'; an old companion never echoes a sig and keeps getting the full list.

title: Two to three SQLite opens per companion request where one is needed
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/api.py:10918 (read_identity_token_ex without conn=), also 2991, 3056, 5607, 11957, 12452; api.py:2623/2629 (identity_bar opens two per mounted fleet API call); api.py:11720 (music_cancel_requested opens music.db on every report)
what: auth._identity_revoked opens its own db.connect (4 PRAGMAs incl. journal_mode=WAL) whenever no connection is passed, although each route already holds one from get_conn; the music cancel lookup opens music.db read-only on every report even with no ingest batch anywhere.
cost: Measured 3 sqlite3.connect per report vs 1 needed, 0.155 ms each locally (more on ZFS with the -shm mapping); at 20 machines x 5 s, about 8 needless opens/s plus one per fleet-job and ingest heartbeat.
evidence: probe_report2.py call-site counter: 200 x _identity_revoked, 200 x music_cancel_requested for 200 reports.
fix: Pass conn=conn at the six call sites; one connection shared by both halves of identity_bar; gate the music/b-roll cancel lookups on an in-process 'a cancel may be pending' flag or short TTL (the heartbeat 410 stays authoritative). Revocation still fails open on a read error.

title: Each light report writes about 28 KB of WAL, much of it re-stamping unchanged state
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/api.py:10984-11015 (clear_report_refused, record_known_editor, record_report_auth, touch_editor_report_token), api.py:11169-11218 (store_* unconditional SET ...=NULL updates), api.py:11352 (replace_active_transfers)
what: A report with nothing new still runs 12 UPDATE, 8 INSERT and 5 DELETE statements; UPDATEs without an IS NOT guard rewrite their page even when values are identical.
cost: Measured 275 WAL frames for 40 reports (~7 pages, 28 KB per report). 4 machines: 160 MB/day idle, 1.9 GB/day syncing at 5 s; 20 machines syncing: ~9.7 GB/day of WAL plus the checkpoint copy, on the snapshotted ZFS dataset. Avoidable share estimated, not measured.
evidence: probe_report4.py: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) -> (0, 275, 275) after 40 reports from a truncated WAL; probe_report5.py statement list.
fix: IS NOT guards on the store_* NULL-setters and the auth/known-editor/token stamps (or coarsen those stamps to once a minute); skip replace_active_transfers when the set is empty and nothing is stored. Keep received_at as the liveness signal and the latch rule that an empty section deletes the row.
